Code block

A block of mono text for a command, a log or a program's output.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For a command the reader may copy, the output of a command, a log, or an excerpt of a file.
  • With the scroll variant when columns must stay aligned, such as a table printed by a tool.
  • With line numbers when the text refers to lines of a file.

When not to use it

  • For a change to a file. Use the diff.
  • For a word or a path inside a sentence. Use a code element in the running text.
  • For a value the reader edits. Use a field.
  • For prose, or to make a message look technical. Mono text is for text a machine wrote or will read.

Variants

wrapping
The default, with no modifier class. Long lines wrap at any character, so nothing is hidden at phone width.
scroll gw-code-block--scroll
Lines keep their length and the body scrolls sideways inside the block. Set tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label on the body.

Accessibility

  • Use a figure holding a pre with a code element inside it. An optional figcaption with the class gw-code-block__caption names what ran or which file it is, and comes first.
  • With the scroll variant, give the pre tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label that says what it holds. It can then take focus, and the arrow keys scroll it. Leave all three off a wrapping block, which never scrolls.
  • For line numbers, give the code element the class gw-code-block__lines and write each line as a gw-code-block__line span holding a gw-code-block__number span and a gw-code-block__text span. The numbers are real text, so a screen reader reads them, and they are left out of a copy.
  • Write the text exactly as the tool printed it. Escape the characters <, > and & in markup.
  • When there is no output, keep the caption and replace the pre with a gw-code-block__note paragraph that says so in a sentence. Never show an empty box.
  • Colour carries no meaning inside a block. A failure is said in the output's own words or in text beside the block.
